title: DESI 2024 IV: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the Lyman Alpha Forest
abstract: arXiv:2404.03001. This paper asks how precisely the first year of DESI data can pin down the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) scale at redshift z > 2, where galaxy surveys run out of tracers and the Lyman-alpha forest in quasar spectra becomes the density probe. The data are DESI DR1 blue-arm spectra: over 420,000 Lyman-alpha forests (twice the SDSS DR16 sample) and more than 700,000 quasars at z > 1.77 as tracers. The method measures four 3D two-point functions (the region-A forest auto-correlation, the region-A x region-B forest correlation, and the cross-correlations of each forest region with quasar positions; the noisy B-region auto-correlation is dropped), fits them jointly with the Vega code including, for the first time, the cross-covariance between auto- and cross-correlations, and marginalises over 15 nuisance parameters for metals, high-column-density absorbers, redshift errors and pipeline noise. The analysis was fully blinded and validated on 150 mocks, data splits and dozens of analysis variations. The result at z_eff = 2.33 is D_H/r_d = 8.52 +/- 0.17 and D_M/r_d = 39.71 +/- 0.95 (2.0% and 2.4% precision), i.e. H(z_eff) = 239.2 +/- 4.8 km/s/Mpc for r_d = 147.09 Mpc, with the cross-correlation now dominating. A combined DESI+SDSS measurement is given too. The authors conclude that one year of DESI already beats ten years of BOSS/eBOSS, and that the largest mock BAO offsets (0.3-0.4%) sit below a conservative 0.5% systematic budget they judge negligible. Left open are non-linear and baryon-velocity shifts in the cross-correlation, more realistic mocks and full-shape analyses.

quote.text: Studies using hydrodynamical simulations have shown that the bias should be small in the Ly α forest auto-correlation [112, 113], but we do not have equivalent studies for the cross-correlation with quasars.

# Executive summary
This paper asks how precisely the first year of DESI data can pin down the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) scale at redshift z > 2, where galaxy surveys run out of tracers and the Lyman-alpha forest in quasar spectra becomes the density probe. The data are DESI DR1 blue-arm spectra: over 420,000 Lyman-alpha forests (twice the SDSS DR16 sample) and more than 700,000 quasars at z > 1.77 as tracers. The analysis was fully blinded and validated on 150 mocks, data splits and dozens of analysis variations. The result at z_eff = 2.33 is D_H/r_d = 8.52 +/- 0.17 and D_M/r_d = 39.71 +/- 0.95 (2.0% and 2.4% precision), i.e. H(z_eff) = 239.2 +/- 4.8 km/s/Mpc for r_d = 147.09 Mpc, with the cross-correlation now dominating. ## Methods
- Four 3D correlation functions (Lya(A)xLya(A), Lya(A)xLya(B), Lya(A)xQSO, Lya(B)xQSO) measured with picca; 15,000 data points, fit over 10 < r < 180 h^-1 Mpc (9,540 bins) with a full covariance including cross-covariance between auto and cross terms.
- Model fit with the Vega package: BAO peak/smooth decomposition, distortion matrix for continuum fitting, plus 15 nuisance parameters (metals, HCDs, correlated sky residuals, quasar redshift errors, proximity effect, small-scale corrections); posteriors sampled with PolyChord, cross-checked with iminuit.
- Fully blinded pipeline: unblinding only after validation on 150 synthetic DR1 realisations (LyaColore and Saclay mocks), data splits, and alternative-analysis variations; broadband polynomial terms shift the best fit by < 0.1 sigma.
- Contaminant handling: DLAs from a combined CNN + Gaussian-process finder masked at > 20% flux decrement; BAL troughs masked rather than lines of sight discarded; C III region used for flux recalibration.
- DESI DR1 posterior combined with the SDSS DR16 (dMdB20) posterior using an approximate cross-survey covariance to give a "DESI + SDSS" BAO measurement.

## Data
- DESI main-survey dark-time quasar spectra from 14 May 2021 to 14 June 2022 (DESI DR1), blue arm only, observed wavelength 3600-5772 A.
- 1,529,530 DR1 quasars passing the selection cuts (ZWARN = 0 or 4); 709,565 with z > 1.77 used as tracers; 428,403 valid region-A forests (1040-1205 A rest frame) and 137,432 region-B forests (920-1020 A).
- Effective redshift z_eff = 2.33; 95% of the auto-correlation signal from 1.96 < z < 2.8 and of the cross-correlation from 1.96 < z < 2.95.
- Most DR1 Lyman-alpha quasars have only a single observation, so spectra are noisier on average than in SDSS DR16.

  loc: "Sec. 6.5"

  quote: "Studies using hydrodynamical simulations have shown that the bias should be small in the Ly α forest auto-correlation [112, 113], but we do not have equivalent studies for the cross-correlation with quasars."
  loc: "Sec. 7.4"
- limit: The DESI + SDSS combination reuses the published dMdB20 posterior with an approximate cross-covariance rather than reanalysing SDSS with the DESI pipeline.
  quote: "It is important to note that we have not redone the SDSS analysis with our analysis pipeline."
  loc: "Sec. 7.3"
- limit: DR1 Lyman-alpha quasars are mostly single-visit and therefore noisier than SDSS DR16 spectra, limiting the auto-correlation's constraining power in this release.

  loc: "Sec. 7.2"
